overview: The Ally Project, featuring poet Terry E. Carter, pianist Jonathan Fagan, bassist Greg Toro, and drummer Gordon Engelgau, performed a set of jazz and spoken-word poetry at the 2026 Medford Jazz Festival. The performance focused on themes of community, West Medford history, gentrification, social justice, and tributes to legendary jazz figures.

items.title: Introduction of the Ally Project
items.summary: Terry Carter introduced the band members and set the theme of social justice and community for the performance.

items.title: Performance of "Hard by the Mystic"
items.summary: Terry Carter performed a poem reflecting on the history, redlining, and gentrification of the West Medford community near the Mystic River.

items.title: Performance of "The Little Store"
items.summary: Terry Carter shared a poem about Mr. Henry's local store, a childhood landmark in West Medford famous for its penny candy.

items.title: Performance of "Corner Lot"
items.summary: The band performed a piece about gentrification, changing demographics, and the enduring history of the Black community at Arlington and Jerome streets.

items.title: Performance of "Beyond Category"
items.summary: Terry Carter and Jonathan Fagan performed a duo piece paying tribute to the life and musical legacy of Duke Ellington.

items.title: Performance of "Reprise for Naima"
items.summary: The group performed a tribute to John Coltrane, exploring his musical style and his love for Naima.

items.title: Performance on Black Representation and Barbie
items.summary: Terry Carter delivered a spoken-word piece imagining a culturally authentic Black Barbie and Ken.

items.title: Performance of "Black Seeds"
items.summary: The band performed a piece addressing political correctness, unapologetic Black identity, history, and resilience.

items.title: Performance of "Blended"
items.summary: Terry Carter and Jonathan Fagan performed a duet about navigating mixed-race identity and cultural belonging.

items.title: Performance of "Neighborhood" and Closing Remarks
items.summary: The band concluded their set with a poem celebrating community solidarity, followed by closing remarks and a call for festival donations.

subject: The Ally Project Performance
